# Judith Chapter 11 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 11 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_011_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Holofernes said to her, "Take courage, woman; do not be afraid in your heart, for I have never harmed anyone who chose to serve Nebuchadnezzar, the king of all the earth.

**2** And now, if your people dwelling in the hill country had not despised me, I would not have raised my spear against them. But they have brought this upon themselves.

**3** Now tell me: why did you flee from them and come to us? You have come to safety. Take courage — you will live this night and from now on.

**4** No one will harm you. All will treat you well, as they do the servants of my lord King Nebuchadnezzar."

**5** Judith said to him, "Accept the words of your servant, and allow your handmaid to speak in your presence. I will speak no falsehood to my lord this night.

**6** If you follow the words of your handmaid, God will bring through you a perfect work, and my lord will not fall short of his purposes.

**7** As Nebuchadnezzar the king of all the earth lives, and as his power lives — who sent you to set every living person in order — not only do human beings serve him through you, but also the beasts of the field, the cattle, and the birds of heaven will live by your strength, under Nebuchadnezzar and all his household.

**8** For we have heard of your wisdom and the skill of your mind; it has been declared throughout all the earth that you alone are worthy in the whole kingdom, mighty in knowledge, and admirable in the craft of war.

**9** Now as for the word that Achior spoke in your council — we have heard his speech. For the men of Bethulia rescued him, and he told them everything he had said before you.

**10** Therefore, O master and lord, do not disregard his word, but take it to heart, for it is true: our people is not punished, and the sword does not prevail against them, unless they sin against their God.

**11** And now, so that my lord may not go away empty-handed and disappointed, death has overtaken them, and sin has gripped them by which they will provoke their God to anger when they act wickedly.

**12** For their food ran short and all their water grew scarce, and they resolved to lay hands on their cattle and decided to consume all the things that God in his laws commanded them not to eat.

**13** The firstfruits of the grain and the tithes of the wine and oil, which they had consecrated and reserved for the priests who minister before the face of our God in Jerusalem — things which no member of the people may even touch with their hands —

**14** they have decided to consume, and they have sent messengers to Jerusalem, since those there have also done the same, to bring back to them authorization from the senate.

**15** And when the word returns to them and they act upon it, they will be handed over to destruction on that very day.

**16** Therefore I your servant, knowing all these things, fled from them, and God sent me to accomplish with you things that will astonish all the earth — as many as hear of them.

**17** For your servant is God-fearing, and I serve the God of heaven day and night; therefore I will remain with you, my lord, and your servant will go out each night into the valley, and I will pray to God, and he will tell me when they have committed their offenses.

**18** And I will come and report it to you, and you will march out with your entire army, and not one of them will stand against you.

**19** And I will guide you through the midst of Judea until you come to Jerusalem; I will set your throne in the midst of it. You will drive them like sheep without a shepherd, and not a dog will open its mouth before you. For this was told to me in accord with my foreknowledge; it was announced to me and I was sent to report it to you."

**20** Her words pleased Holofernes and all his servants, and they marveled at her wisdom, saying,

**21** "There is no woman like her from one end of the earth to the other — so beautiful of face and so wise of speech."

**22** Holofernes said to her, "God has done well to send you ahead of the people, so that power may rest in our hands and ruin come upon those who have contemned my lord.

**23** And now you are beautiful in your appearance and fine in your words. If you do as you have said, your God shall be my God, and you shall live in the household of King Nebuchadnezzar and be celebrated throughout all the earth."

---
*LOGOS notes: "Senate" for gerousia (v. 14) reflects the Hellenistic institution of a council of elders. "God-fearing" (theosebes) is rendered as a single adjective in v. 17. Judith's entire speech is crafted with careful ambiguity — she speaks in double meanings understood one way by Holofernes, another way by the reader.*
